sources_considered.why: Direct 2022 experiments test GPT-3 addition under equivalent formatting changes and alternative prompts.
The pre-publication version reports systematic symbolic and arithmetic failures, alongside successful assisted methods.
Read to verify the original submission date and the scope of the reported findings.
The original GPT-3 evaluation predates the selected contemporary period; more directly relevant 2022 experiments were available.

evidence_items.publisher: MIT CSAIL research blog; Ekin Akyürek and Afra Feyza Akyürek
evidence_items.locator: Analysis, When do scratchpads help?, immediately after Figure 2
evidence_items.explanation: The researchers tested code_davinci_002 on 100 number pairs per digit length and found that changing number formatting disrupted few-shot addition. This is evidence against fully general application of the underlying arithmetic rule.

evidence_items.locator: Section 1, discussion of Figure 2 and the copy task
evidence_items.explanation: Controlled symbolic tests show failures beyond the demonstrated distribution, including problems with repeated symbols. These failures support incomplete systematic generalization in the contemporary GPT model.

The paper also reports improvements from callable programs and perfect tested performance with its tutor method. These results qualify any suggestion of inherent impossibility, but assisted success on finite tests does not establish full mastery by the unassisted model.
